_about: Retiming of the powers-of-ten zoom (tools/powers-of-ten/zoom-timeline.js, in the author's zoom source) to its narration (rec52, 2026-11-03; video/short-00-powers-of-ten/). `at` is the video time, in seconds, at which the zoom should be framing `shows`: the moment the narration names it (the first word of its name). frameWidthM is a rough frame width, for keys the timeline doesn't have yet. Join the keys with the timeline's smooth curve (no stops between them), stop on the Planck grid at the 'planck' key and hold the gliders from there to the end, 180 s. The narration ends at speechEnd.

keys.line: As far as we've been able to measure…
The largest thing we can see is the cosmic microwave background…
The smaller bubble inside is the cosmic event horizon…
Inside them are the largest structures of all: superclusters…
We live in one such small filament called the Laniakea supercluster…
And in here, we see our local neighbourhood of galaxies.
Here's Andromeda…
…and here's the Milky Way: that's us.
And in one of its arms, one star among hundreds of billions is the Sun.
Here are the nearby stars, Sirius and Proxima Centauri.
The Sun is surrounded by billions of icy comets that make up the Oort cloud.
Now we can see the orbits of planets…
…and the third rock from the Sun: that's home.

keys.shows: Earth and the Moon going by
keys.line: We see the Moon zoom by.
And in North America,
California,
in the Sierra Nevada,
…lives the forest of giant sequoias.
And there lives the General Sherman, the largest tree on Earth.
And on one of its branches, a ladybug…
…is drinking a little bit of morning dew.
And we find our first single-celled organism: an amoeba.

keys.shows: the cell's nucleus, then its DNA
keys.line: Inside it, we find its nucleus, and its DNA, wound tight around proteins.
The double helix is two millionths of a millimetre wide.
Atom is Greek for uncuttable…

keys.shows: the atom's empty space, the electron cloud
keys.line: They're made of electrons, protons and neutrons, and they're mostly empty space.
And the proton and neutron, in turn, are made of smaller things, like quarks and gluons.
And what are quarks made of? Well, truly, we don't know.

keys.shows: the quark patterns into the grey terrain
keys.line: But now, instead of searching for the smallest building block…
Quantum field theory describes the universe as simply numbers at every point…
Our journey ends at the Planck length.
At this point, relativity clashes with quantum mechanics.
Is that the limit? … it's all one big game of life.
